Article Title: New car safety rules: Rear-crash tests from 2029 to prevent fire, immobilisers from 2027
Article Text:
New norms for cars from 2029: Rear-crashtests, data recorders

NEW DELHI: Aiming to prevent fires caused by rear-end collisions, all new cars manufactured from April 2029 will have to comply with a crash-test standard that ensures no fuel spillage or damage to the battery in petrol/diesel and electric vehicles, respectively. The road transport ministry has made compliance with this automotive industry standard mandatory.“To meet the norm, cars will have to be designed and manufactured in a way that prevents damage to the fuel tank or battery in a rear-end collision,” an official said.The ministry has also set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards.In a notification, the ministry has also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from October 2029. EDRs remain optional but record crash-related data to help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. Their function is similar to that of an aircraft’s flight-data recorder, or black box.“The rollout will be phased, as the data can help assess driving behaviour and identify corrective measures to prevent future crashes,” the official said.He added that mandatory fitment of immobilisers in cars from October 2027 would be crucial to preventing vehicle theft. An immobiliser is an electronic anti-theft device that prevents an engine from starting unless it detects the correct key or an authorised electronic signal.
Article Summary: All new cars manufactured from April 2029 will have to comply with a crash-test standard that ensures no fuel spillage or damage to the battery in petrol/diesel and electric vehicles. The road transport ministry has made compliance with this automotive industry standard mandatory. The ministry has also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from October 2029.

Article Title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
Article Text:
The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds using Indian numbers

NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone. The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the app’s functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding “that some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,” a statement read.To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is “continuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.” And also ensure that “web service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code. ”
Article Summary: From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card.

Article Title: Oppo Find X10, Find X10 Pro Max launched with 200MP cameras, 8,000mAh battery

Oppo India has launched the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max smartphones, expanding its flagship phone lineup with 200MP cameras, batteries of up to 8,000mAh and new AI features. Both phones run ColorOS 17 and support 80W wired and 50W wireless charging. The Find X10 comes with two 200MP rear cameras, while the Find X10 Pro Max features three. Oppo has also introduced the Pad Mini tablet, Enco X4 earbuds and a 10,000mAh power bank as part of its connected device lineup. Here’s a look at the features, price and availability of Oppo Find X10 Pro and Oppo Find X10 Pro Max.Oppo Find X10 features a 6.59-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 3,600 nits. The screen supports Dolby Vision and can dim to 1 nit for viewing in low-light conditions. The smartphone has a glass design and will be available in Glacier Blue, Glow Coral and Mist Grey. It also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for water and dust resistance under specified test conditions.The Find X10 features a dual 200MP rear camera system developed with Hasselblad. Oppo's LUMO True Image Engine is designed to improve colour reproduction, tones and image details.The phone supports 4K video recording at 60fps across all rear cameras. Its main and telephoto cameras can also record 4K video at 120fps and 8K video at 30fps.Users can capture 50MP or 200MP images through Hasselblad Hi-Res Mode on supported cameras. The phone is also compatible with the Oppo Hasselblad Teleconverter, which offers 3.28x optical magnification.Oppo Find X10 is powered by the 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600M processor. It packs a silicon-carbon battery of up to 8,000mAh and supports 80W SUPERVOOC wired charging and 50W AIRVOOC wireless charging. The phone also features vapour chamber cooling to manage heat during gaming, photography and other demanding tasks.The handset runs ColorOS 17, which introduces AI Mind Pilot with Agent Mode. The feature can work with photos and files stored on the phone to search for information and complete tasks involving multiple steps. AI Photo Agent offers photo-editing suggestions and supports text instructions. Its Style Match feature can apply the look of a reference image to a user's photo. The software also includes AI Call Guard, which uses on-device AI to identify possible signs of fraud during calls.Oppo Find X10 Pro Max features three 200MP rear cameras: an ultra-wide camera, a main camera and a telephoto camera. The 200MP ultra-wide camera has a 124-degree field of view and a 1/1.56-inch sensor. The 200MP main camera uses a 1/1.28-inch sensor developed by Oppo and Samsung, along with DeepPix technology to improve HDR performance. The 200MP telephoto camera has an f/2.1 aperture and supports close-up photography from a minimum focusing distance of 10cm.The phone supports 4K video recording at 60fps and 120fps, as well as 8K recording at 30fps, across all three rear cameras. It also supports Dolby Vision, O-Log2 and Open Gate Capture for video recording and editing.The Find X10 Pro Max features a 6.78-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 3,600 nits. It supports Dolby Vision and can dim to 1 nit, with 3,840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming. The phone will be available in Titanium Grey and Luna White. Both colours feature a glass design, with the Luna White variant drawing inspiration from traditional cameras through its two-tone finish and orange accent ring.The device also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for water and dust resistance under specified test conditions.The Find X10 Pro Max runs on the 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro processor. Like the Find X10, it has a silicon-carbon battery of up to 8,000mAh, with support for 80W wired and 50W wireless charging.Oppo Find X10 Pro Max also runs ColorOS 17, with AI Mind Pilot with Agent Mode and AI Photo Agent. These features help users search information stored on the device, complete multi-step tasks and edit photos using text instructions.Oppo's software also includes AI Call Guard and Private Computing Cloud, which uses encryption and other security measures for cloud-based AI processing.Oppo has also launched the Pad Mini, its first compact 8.8-inch tablet. It weighs 282g, measures 5.46mm in thickness and features a 2.5K OLED display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz and peak brightness of 1,600 nits.The tablet runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor and packs an 8,000mAh battery with 67W SUPERVOOC charging. It supports connectivity with iOS, Android and Windows devices through O+ Connect.The Pad Mini is also compatible with the Oppo Pencil 3 Pro, which supports writing, sketching, Screen-Off Quick Notes and Doodle to Art features.Oppo Enco X4 earbuds feature a dual-driver audio system developed with Dynaudio. Other features include AI Clear Call, Conversation Awareness, sleep tracking and neck health monitoring.They offer up to 53 hours of total battery life and support connections to two devices. Article Title: Airtel partners with YouTube to offer Premium benefits to prepaid
Article Text:
YouTube Premium now part of Airtel's entertainment ecosystem

Available through Rs 200 OTT top-up

Focus on changing content consumption habits

Telecom operator Airtel has announced a partnership with YouTube to bring YouTube Premium benefits to its prepaid customers, adding the video platform's premium offering to its growing portfolio of entertainment services. The company said the move is aimed at addressing changing consumer behaviour, where mobile data is increasingly being used not only for communication but also for video streaming, music listening, creator-led content consumption and content discovery.Under the partnership, Airtel prepaid customers will be able to access YouTube Premium benefits, including an ad-free YouTube experience, background playback, offline downloads and YouTube Music Premium. The telecom operator said the addition of YouTube Premium strengthens its entertainment proposition by expanding beyond traditional OTT video streaming services.Airtel noted that YouTube Premium joins a list of entertainment offerings already available through its OTT portfolio, which includes Prime Video, JioHotstar, ZEE5 Premium, SonyLIV and more than 18 other OTT platforms.The YouTube Premium benefit will be bundled with Airtel's Rs 200 OTT top-up pack, which also includes 30GB of additional data.The company said the offering is available to Airtel prepaid customers who have an active base recharge plan.Customers can activate the benefit through the "Rewards & OTTs" section of the Airtel Thanks app after purchasing the top-up.According to Airtel, the partnership reflects evolving smartphone usage trends, with customers increasingly relying on mobile data to watch videos, follow creators, catch up on entertainment content, stream music and discover new digital experiences.The company said the inclusion of YouTube Premium broadens its prepaid entertainment portfolio and brings together multiple forms of content consumption under a single offering, ranging from OTT streaming and creator content to music and short-form videos.Airtel said the YouTube Premium benefit will remain active for the duration of the top-up's 28-day validity period. Once the top-up expires, customers who wish to continue using the service can purchase the pack again and re-claim the YouTube Premium benefit through the Airtel app.The company added that by combining data, premium entertainment subscriptions and other digital services in one package, it aims to provide greater value to prepaid subscribers beyond basic connectivity.
Article Summary: Airtel has announced a partnership with YouTube to bring YouTube Premium benefits to its prepaid customers. The move is aimed at addressing changing consumer behaviour. Mobile data is increasingly being used for video streaming, music listening, creator-led content consumption and content discovery.

Article Title: Meet Ellianna Gu, the Salt Lake City eighth-grader who tested ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini on 84 teen emotional scenarios and found their replies often lacked empathy
Article Text:

How Ellianna Gu tested the three chatbots

What the results showed

“I think that the human brain is really fascinating and I would love to learn more about it,”

“I also want to help people, especially those suffering from life-altering conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s disease.”

A teenager has tested AI chatbots' ability to handle teenage emotions. Ellianna Gu, an eighth-grader from Utah's Salt Lake City, examined responses from OpenAI ’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google Gemini. She chose this test after learning that some teenagers were turning to these services for friendship and emotional support. Her project used 84 scenarios involving academic stress, social anxiety, friendship problems, family conflict, loneliness, anger and sadness. Gu found that the chatbots generally produced clear and structured answers, but their replies did not display much empathy. Their performance also changed depending on whether a scenario was written formally or with slang, indicating that writing style could affect the support a teenager received.The project, titledmade Gu a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. She developed the study after reading earlier research that raised concerns about how chatbots respond to people seeking emotional support.u said.Gu first used AI to create realistic situations based on seven types of emotional challenges commonly faced by teenagers. She varied the language in the prompts, including both slang and more formal writing, before submitting all 84 scenarios to ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.She then evaluated the replies using four criteria: empathy, clarity, problem-solving and helpfulness. Most categories were scored on a scale of one to three, while empathy was rated on a scale of one to four.Gu assessed the answers manually and also used AI to analyse them. This allowed her to compare the chatbots’ responses using both human judgment and an automated evaluation.The three chatbots generally provided organised and understandable responses. However, Gu found that their answers often lacked empathy, an important quality when responding to a teenager discussing loneliness, anxiety or another emotional concern. The systems also reacted differently depending on how a prompt was written. A scenario expressed through slang could produce a different response than one describing the same problem in formal language.Their effectiveness scores were also limited. According to the project summary, among the three services, only Claude received a score of three for effectiveness. Outside the competition, Gu plays the piano and clarinet and hopes to become a neurologist.she said.

Gu found that the chatbots generally produced clear and structured answers, but their replies did not display much empathy.

Article Title: Fake faces, stolen voices, false stories: Can we still trust what we see online?
Article Text:
Recent incidents highlight how Artificial Intelligence can create deceptive videos and audio that mislead individuals (AI image)

High-profile figures are increasingly targeted by tech-driven scams.

Real-life incidents that show we can no longer believe everything we see online

1. Rashmika Mandanna's deepfake video — November 2023

October 8, 2023: An original video featuring social media personality Zara Patel was posted on Instagram.

An original video featuring social media personality Zara Patel was posted on Instagram. November 7, 2023: A manipulated version featuring Rashmika Mandanna's face went viral online.

A manipulated version featuring Rashmika Mandanna's face went viral online. November 10–11, 2023: Delhi Police registered an FIR and began investigating the circulation of the video.

2. AI voice-cloning scam targeting a mother — March 2024

March 18, 2024: A mother from Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, received a phone call claiming that her daughter had been kidnapped.

A mother from Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, received a phone call claiming that her daughter had been kidnapped. The caller used a voice resembling her daughter's and demanded ₹3 lakh as ransom.

The frightened mother transferred ₹50,000 before discovering that her daughter was safe in her hostel.

3. Fake investment video featuring Nirmala Sitharaman — November 2024

November 21, 2024: A manipulated video falsely portrayed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das as endorsing an investment scheme.

A manipulated video falsely portrayed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das as endorsing an investment scheme. The video promoted unrealistic financial returns and used manipulated footage and AI-generated audio.

Fact-checkers established that the officials had not endorsed the scheme.

It is essential for individuals to adopt cautious practices to combat misinformation effectively

Understanding the rise of digital deception

AI videos: When the camera can lie

Fake news and the speed of misinformation

Voice-cloning scams: Hearing is not believing

How to spot misleading content

Check the source: Look for the original publisher and check whether reputable news organisations have reported the same information.

Look for the original publisher and check whether reputable news organisations have reported the same information. Verify the context: Check the date, location, and circumstances in which a video or image was supposedly recorded.

Check the date, location, and circumstances in which a video or image was supposedly recorded. Look for inconsistencies: Unnatural facial movements, strange lighting, mismatched lip movements, or unusual audio may indicate manipulation, although modern deepfakes may not show obvious flaws.

Unnatural facial movements, strange lighting, mismatched lip movements, or unusual audio may indicate manipulation, although modern deepfakes may not show obvious flaws. Use reverse image searches: Searching for an image can help reveal whether it appeared earlier in a different context.

Searching for an image can help reveal whether it appeared earlier in a different context. Read beyond the headline: Sensational headlines may exaggerate or misrepresent the actual content of a report.

Sensational headlines may exaggerate or misrepresent the actual content of a report. Pause before sharing: If a claim seems shocking or emotionally charged, verify it before forwarding it to others.

If a claim seems shocking or emotionally charged, verify it before forwarding it to others. Confirm through another channel: For suspicious voice messages or urgent requests for money, contact the person directly using a trusted phone number.

Digital awareness builds trust and accountability online.

What can social media platforms do?

Conclusion: Trust, but verify





For decades, people have been holding on to the idea that seeing is believing. Photographs were believed to be the evidence of something happening, videos were believed to be the proof of something, and the known voice on a phone call would prove a person’s identity. However, nowadays, these notions seem to lose their reliability. Artificial intelligence (AI) can produce videos of individuals saying things that they never said, can produce voices using a brief audio recording, and can produce photos of things that did not happen.In times when news spreads all over the world in seconds, differentiating the truth from the fiction becomes a difficult task. Videos shared via WhatsApp, voice messages from family members, and posts on the Internet featuring a famous political leader might be authentic, but they are fake.This is not just a problem of modern technology. This is about a threat for people’s safety, freedom of democracy, credibility of journalism, and the overall public trust.The incident raised serious concerns about privacy, online misinformation and the misuse of AI technology. It demonstrated how a person could be falsely portrayed in a video without their knowledge or consent.This incident demonstrated how scammers can use AI-generated voices to exploit people's emotions and trick them into transferring money.The incident highlighted how fraudsters can misuse the images and voices of public figures to make fraudulent investment schemes appear trustworthy.These incidents show that videos can be manipulated, voices can be cloned and public figures can be falsely portrayed as endorsing fraudulent schemes. They establish why online content must be verified rather than accepted at face value.Artificial intelligence has made it easier than ever to create realistic images, videos, and audio recordings. Deepfake technology can imitate a person’s face, expressions, and voice, making it difficult for viewers to identify whether a video is genuine. At the same time, fake news can spread rapidly through social media, often reaching thousands of people before the truth is established.These developments are concerning because people often trust what they can see and hear. A video of a public figure making a statement or an audio recording of a familiar voice may appear to be reliable evidence, even when it has been manipulated or completely fabricated.AI-generated videos, commonly known as deepfakes, can make people appear to say or do things that never happened. While this technology can be used for entertainment, education, and filmmaking, it can also be misused to spread misinformation, damage reputations, and influence public opinion.For example, a fabricated video of a political leader making a controversial statement could circulate widely before fact-checkers have time to verify it. Even after the video is exposed as fake, the damage may already have been done. Some viewers may continue to believe the original claim, while others may lose trust in genuine recordings.Fake news is not new, but digital platforms have made it easier to create and distribute misleading stories at an extraordinary speed. Sensational headlines, edited images, and false claims can attract attention and be shared before users check their accuracy.Algorithms that recommend engaging content can sometimes contribute to the spread of misinformation. When people repeatedly encounter similar claims, they may begin to accept them as true, even when reliable evidence is missing.The problem is not limited to completely fabricated stories. Genuine photographs and videos can also be taken out of context, edited, or paired with misleading captions to create a false impression.AI voice-cloning tools can reproduce a person’s voice using relatively small amounts of audio. Scammers can exploit this technology to impersonate family members, company executives, or other trusted individuals.Imagine receiving a phone call from someone who sounds exactly like a family member asking for urgent financial help. The familiar voice may make the request seem genuine, causing the listener to act without checking the facts.To protect themselves, people should verify unusual requests through another communication channel, avoid sharing sensitive information over unexpected calls, and be cautious when someone pressures them to transfer money urgently.Although AI-generated content is becoming more realistic, there are still steps people can take to assess whether something online is trustworthy.No single method can identify every deepfake or misleading post. The most reliable approach is to combine careful observation with independent verification.Social media platforms have an important role in limiting the spread of deceptive content. They can improve systems for detecting manipulated media, label AI-generated content when appropriate, and provide clear information about the origin of images, videos, and audio recordings.Platforms can also work with independent fact-checkers, respond more quickly to reports of harmful misinformation, and make it easier for users to understand why particular content is being recommended. Greater transparency about how content is created and distributed can help people make better-informed decisions.However, automated detection systems are not perfect. Platforms must balance the need to reduce harmful misinformation with the importance of protecting legitimate expression, satire, journalism, and creative uses of AI.Governments, technology companies, news organisations, and users all have a role to play in building a more trustworthy digital environment.As AI technology continues to advance, the boundary between real and fake content will become increasingly difficult to identify. Videos, photographs, and voices can no longer be accepted as unquestionable proof simply because they appear authentic.The solution is not to distrust everything online, but to develop stronger habits of digital awareness. By checking sources, verifying claims, and thinking carefully before sharing information, users can reduce the risk of being misled.In a world where seeing is no longer believing, critical thinking and responsible sharing are essential. Technology may make deception easier, but awareness and verification can help us protect the truth.
Article Summary: Recent incidents highlight how Artificial Intelligence can create deceptive videos and audio that mislead individuals (AI image) High-profile figures are increasingly targeted by tech-driven scams. Real-life incidents that show we can no longer believe everything we see online include Rashmika Mandanna's deepfake video.

Article Title: Nebraska workers cut 150 trees from crowded lake banks and sank them at 16 underwater locations; the September 2026 project is building shelter for young fish in two lakes without using concrete reefs
Article Text:
How trees become underwater fish shelters

Clearing crowded banks improves fishing access

Part of a wider habitat restoration effort

Can the new habitat help fish populations?

Instead of building concrete reefs, conservation workers in Nebraska have turned trees cleared from overgrown lake banks into underwater fish habitats, placing around 150 trees at 16 locations across two lakes. The project, completed in September 2026, aims to give smaller fish places to hide from predators while improving fishing access along the shore. According to the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission, the trees were transported and submerged using a new Aquatic Habitat Barge at Bridgeport State Recreation Area.The project used approximately 60 cedar and Russian olive trees at five locations in the recreation area's southeast lake and another 90 trees at 11 locations in the middle lake. The trees were removed from crowded shoreline areas, allowing crews to address two problems at once: overgrown banks that restricted access for anglers and a shortage of underwater woody habitat for fish.The commission announced the work on October 22, explaining that the brush piles would provide shelter for smaller fish and help support the aquatic food web. The project is part of Nebraska's wider effort to improve lake habitats and make fishing more productive.Trees that might otherwise be removed as shoreline vegetation can serve another purpose once submerged. Their branches and trunks create a network of spaces where small fish can hide, making it harder for larger predatory fish to reach them. The underwater structures also provide surfaces where algae and other organisms can grow. These can attract plankton and small aquatic creatures, which in turn become food for fish. The resulting chain of interactions helps support a wider aquatic food web.The Nebraska Game and Parks Commission said the brush piles are intended to benefit fish populations and anglers by improving habitat conditions. However, the announcement does not provide post-project monitoring data demonstrating a measured increase in fish numbers at the two lakes. The trees are not simply dumped into the water at random. Crews transport and position them at selected underwater locations, while the commission makes approximate placement information available through its lake habitat and structure maps. These help anglers identify underwater features that may attract fish.The project also illustrates how vegetation removed for one practical reason can be reused to address a different environmental need.The work has a benefit beyond the underwater ecosystem. The cedar and Russian olive trees were cut from overgrown shoreline areas, opening up sections of the banks for anglers. Shoreline vegetation can restrict access to the water, particularly at locations where trees and branches have grown densely. Removing selected trees can make it easier for people to reach the water's edge while allowing some of the same material to be reused as fish habitat.Bridgeport State Recreation Area, located in western Nebraska, covers approximately 326 acres, including 78 acres of water spread across five sandpit lakes. The area offers fishing, boating, camping, swimming and other outdoor activities, according to the state agency. Its waters support several fish species, including largemouth bass, walleye, bluegill, yellow perch and channel catfish. Rainbow trout are also stocked in some of the area's lakes. Improving underwater habitat can help fisheries managers maintain suitable conditions for fish while making recreational waters more useful to visitors.Nebraska has been using a range of approaches to improve aquatic habitats, including submerged trees, artificial fish attractors and rock structures. The Nebraska Game and Parks Commission's Aquatic Habitat Program was established in 1997. According to the agency, it has generated more than $90 million for improvements to 137 water bodies across the state. The programme supports projects intended to improve aquatic conditions, fisheries and recreational access.A 2026 overview published by Nebraskaland Magazine, the commission's outdoor publication, describes other efforts involving woody habitat. At 11 lakes along Interstate 80, invasive eastern red cedar and Russian olive trees were removed to improve shoreline access, with some of the cut trees placed in the lakes to create fish habitat.The state has also used rock shoals at other reservoirs. In partnership with the US Bureau of Reclamation, 42 shoals were built at Medicine Creek Reservoir in 2025, following the construction of 43 at Swanson Reservoir in 2023. These structures provide underwater habitat in areas that otherwise offer relatively few features for fish.The different projects show that habitat restoration does not depend on a single design. Depending on the water body and its needs, managers can use woody material, rocks or purpose-built structures to increase habitat diversity. The Bridgeport project specifically uses trees rather than newly constructed rock structures. However, the commission has not described it as a formal replacement for concrete reefs, and the wider state programme continues to use other habitat-building methods where appropriate.The immediate objective is to create places where smaller fish can escape predators and where food organisms can gather. Such structures can make underwater environments more complex, providing fish with shelter and feeding opportunities that may be scarce in open areas.The commission expects the improved habitat to support healthier fish populations and better fishing opportunities. Whether the new brush piles produce a measurable increase in fish abundance at Bridgeport will depend on factors including water conditions, food availability, predation and the long-term use of the structures by different species.The state has made the approximate locations of the newly installed brush piles available through its lake contour and habitat maps, allowing anglers to find the underwater structures.For now, the September project offers a practical example of how clearing overgrown shorelines can do more than improve access. By placing the cut trees beneath the water, Nebraska's fisheries managers have converted vegetation into a resource intended to support fish, aquatic food webs and recreational fishing.
Article Summary: Trees were removed from overgrown shoreline areas at two lakes in Nebraska. They were submerged to provide underwater habitat for fish. The project is part of a wider effort to improve lake habitats and make fishing more productive. The state has also used rock shoals at other reservoirs.

Citrus waste also requires careful handling

Evaluating the Pollution Risk of Soil Due to Natural Drainage of Orange Peel: First Results

Orange peel, a common citrus-processing by-product, was shredded and mixed into the topsoil in the Italian erosion trial. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Further field testing is needed

Soil erosion can gradually strip away the fertile surface layer that plants depend on, especially on steep land exposed to heavy rainfall. Protection of slope areas has remained an issue to be solved by farmers and landowners. Several studies have been done to check whether agricultural residues, normally wasted after processing the food materials, can provide a solution to this problem. A 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues in southern Italy checked whether solar-dried citrus peel could help control runoff and soil erosion. The study results indicated that orange peel, which is normally left after producing juice, was effective in reducing soil erosion.According to Bombino and colleagues’ 2010 paper on land spreading of solar-dried citrus peel, the experiment used eight plots, each measuring 2 square metres, arranged in two wooden boxes set at a 100% slope. In four plots, the researchers added citrus peel, while the remaining four were left untreated. The 100% slope indicates that the vertical rise is the same as the horizontal distance. Solar-dried citrus peel was shredded into small pieces (4 to 8 mm) and mixed into the top 3 cm of soil at a rate of 3 kg per square metre. Then, the plots were subjected to natural rainfall and the researchers were able to observe runoff and sediment loss in treated and untreated soils under field conditions.The experiment was conducted during 20 rain events. Different rainfall conditions and plots with different ground cover properties were observed.According to Bombino and colleagues, the key result was a 50% reduction in soil erosion in the treated plots compared with the controls. There was a 10% average decrease in the surface runoff as well. During this experiment, sediment yield and sediment concentration were, on average, 55-60% less in treated plots than in the controls. The decrease in runoff varied depending on observations and reached up to 33% at maximum. Runoff is the water flowing over the soil surface, whereas sediment yield is the soil carried out of the plot. In other words, despite the small decrease in runoff volumes, the decrease in soil loss may be much higher. The results suggest that solar-dried citrus peel can help minimize erosion under the tested conditions. Yet, it does not mean that the same effect will take place under other conditions.The study authors hypothesized that adding citrus peel would improve soil quality and promote plant growth. Organic material affects soil structure and the passage of water and could thus aid in the passage of rainwater into the soil instead of running on top of it. Plants are able to act as a shield from raindrops and slow down surface water. Plant roots might also play a role in keeping soil particles bound together. Improved soil quality and plant development were two possible explanations offered for decreased erosion. This interpretation needs to be carefully qualified. While there were clear distinctions made between treated and untreated plots in the experiment, there was no way of proving the degree to which each potential mechanism contributed to the decreased erosion.Using citrus peel on land could provide a useful outlet for waste from fruit-processing industries. However, applying organic waste to soil also requires consideration of what happens as it decomposes and releases liquid. A later study,, published in Environments in 2021, investigated the potential pollution risk associated with drainage from orange peel. In their study, the scientists studied the organic liquid that came out of the substance under the conditions of the experiment. The authors concluded that the risk of soil pollution from natural drainage of orange peel was negligible, given the limited amounts of leachate and organic load, although they noted that heavy rainfall could aggravate the hazard.The paper reports three lysimeter tests on orange peel: one with raw peel left to drain naturally and two others exposed to 100 mm of simulated rainfall after the peel had already drained or been solar-dried. In about 14 weeks, the peel volume fell by roughly 90% and the raw-peel test released 37.7 L of leachate, about 19% of the initial peel volume. The authors found that the organic load reaching the soil was negligible. Unlike the erosion study conducted in 2010, this study raises a new question. In combination, the studies show the need to consider both the advantages and disadvantages of using agricultural waste.The 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues suggests that solar-dried citrus peel can reduce soil erosion, but only under the specific experimental conditions tested. This information could be useful in any attempt to preserve lands which are either steep or erosion-prone, as well as discovering other uses for by-products from agriculture. Nevertheless, the experiment was carried out on a relatively small number of plots under certain conditions in southern Italy. Further research is needed to test the treatment in different soil types and climates and to assess how long the effect lasts. For now, the study only suggests that citrus peel may be useful in soil conservation, not that it is a guaranteed solution. The actual applicability of the material will depend on its efficiency in real-life situations.
Article Summary: Soil erosion can gradually strip away the fertile surface layer that plants depend on, especially on steep land exposed to heavy rainfall. A 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues in southern Italy checked whether solar-dried citrus peel could help control runoff and soil erosion. The study results indicated that orange peel, which is normally left after producing juice, was effective in reducing erosion.

Article Title: In the late 2000s, while inspecting reefs on Google Earth, specialist Chris Simpson spotted rare reefs off Australia’s remote Kimberley coast, revealing marine habitats that had been poorly mapped
Article Text:
AI Representation: In 2007, Chris Simpson discovered rare, poorly mapped reefs off Australia’s remote Kimberley coast using Google Earth. Image credits: Chatgpt

Chris Simpson’s Google Earth sighting of fringing reefs

Why the Kimberley coast had limited public coral data before 2009

Biodiversity

and biogeography of zooxanthellate corals in Australasia revisited based on new data from the Kimberley

Montgomery Reef, a coral-reef hotspot on Western Australia’s remote Kimberley coast. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Museum surveys from 2009 to 2014 and the count of 438 coral species

The

2015 Bonaparte Archipelago study

and the question of bleaching resilience

A diverse assemblage of reef corals thriving in a dynamic intertidal reef setting (Bonaparte Archipelago, Kimberley, Australia)

Coral reef specialists have long relied on satellite imagery to study reefs that are costly and difficult to reach by boat. Dr. Chris Simpson, a government scientist in Western Australia, regularly searched Google Earth for reefs along the state’s northern coast. On one such occasion, late in 2007, he discovered an extensive formation of fringing coral reefs off the remote Kimberley coast, a sight The Age described as rarely seen anywhere in the world. The Kimberley Development Commission describes the Kimberley as remot and the NASA Earth Observatory notes that the Kimberley coast has some of the largest tidal ranges in Australia and ranks among the largest in the world, with water levels at Montgomery Reef dropping sharply at low tide. Limited information was available about the reefs in this area, highlighting how little of the coastline had been documented.Dr. Chris Simpson, a coral reef specialist at Western Australia’s Department of Environment and Conservation, made the sighting, as ReefBuilders reported on February 13, 2008. A report in The Age, republished by Climate Shifts, places the sighting late in 2007.Simpson could identify reefs in Landsat images and aerial photographs before Google Earth launched in 2005. The platform later made it easier to view the area without having to piece together separate images. The mapping blog Ogle Earth traced the sighting to places like the Buccaneer Archipelago and Cape Bougainville.The study, published in the Records of the Western Australian Museum , describes a complex array of nearshore platform and fringing reefs along an estimated 12,000 kilometres of the northern Western Australian coastline, which suggests the Kimberley is an exception to the worldwide scarcity of fringing reefs noted earlier and describes the region as isolated from urban centres. According to the authors of the paper, Zoe Richards, Michel Pichon and Carden Wallace, the lack of information in the public domain hindered efforts to confirm the expected richness of the area in terms of its coral cover.Working in this environment is not easy. The above-mentioned study reports inshore tidal oscillations of more than 11 metres, strong currents and murky water, which limited subtidal diving to roughly 45 minutes around slack high tide. The surveys covered inshore, mid-shelf and offshore reefs, but they left gaps, because the discussion section notes that only islands and reefs at least 10 kilometres from the mainland were surveyed, so corals closer to shore remain poorly documented.The Field surveys section of the above mentioned study records coral sampling at 171 stations between 2009 and 2014. Of these, 135 stations had transect belts; a total of 491 transects were conducted and 19,086 coral colonies were counted. At the remaining 36 stations, the same section notes that corals were collected incidentally during rapid visual assessment surveys. Combining the new museum-accessioned specimen records with recent donations and published historical records from 1893 onwards, the above-mentioned study puts the regional total at 438 zooxanthellate reef-building coral species, up from an estimate of 350 species made by Veron and colleagues in 2015. The above-mentioned study extended the known distribution of 85 species in the region, 37 of which are new records for Australia and identified Ashmore Reef, Cassini Island and Montgomery Reef as regional coral biodiversity hotspots.A separate paper,, appeared in PLOS ONE in 2015. As its abstract notes, the study documents for the first time an assemblage of 225 hard coral species in the intertidal zone of the Bonaparte Archipelago and presents it as a cause for some optimism because the corals thrive in an unusually harsh setting. The museum study returns to the question of resilience. It notes that the central and northern Kimberley reefs appear to have largely resisted widespread bleaching and mortality so far and suggests that the extreme conditions their corals routinely experience make these reefs a natural laboratory for examining the traits that confer resilience. The study frames this against the 2016 to 2017 bleaching event, which severely affected the Far Northern Great Barrier Reef, Australia’s most renowned repository of coral diversity and argues that this makes identifying other caches of diversity increasingly important.
Article Summary: In 2007, Chris Simpson discovered rare, poorly mapped reefs off Australia’s remote Kimberley coast using Google Earth. Limited information was available about the reefs in this area, highlighting how little of the coastline had been documented. Simpson could identify reefs in Landsat images and aerial photographs before Google Earth launched in 2005. The study describes a complex array of nearshore platform and fringing reefs along an estimated 12,000 kilometres of the northern Western Australian coastline.

Article Title: A 19-year-old Australian farmer’s son developed a drone system for moving cattle; his startup raised $1.2 million to expand
Article Text:
PC: Forbes

How does the Australian farmer’s son’s drone system move cattle

How does GrazeMate’s drone system collect farm and cattle data

How did GrazeMate raise $1.2 million to expand into California

How did the GrazeMate founder develop his engineering and AI skills

Climbing in the Everest region inspired cattle-mustering technology

AI advances and drone technology helping expand cattle mustering

A 19-year-old Australian farmer’s son has developed an autonomous drone system to move cattle, with his startup, GrazeMate, raising $1.2 million in pre-seed funding to support its expansion into California. Founded by Sam Rogers, the company uses drones that farmers can operate through a mobile app to guide herds between paddocks without manually piloting the aircraft. According to Forbes Australia, GrazeMate has commitments to muster 1.7 million acres across Queensland and New South Wales. The system also collects information on pasture availability, estimated herd weight and farm infrastructure, including water troughs.Rogers described the system as a way for farmers to select a paddock through an app and dispatch a drone to move a herd. He explained, “GrazeMate lets a farmer open an app, select a paddock, and send a drone out to move the herd.” The system is designed to notify the farmer when the cattle have passed through the gate, reducing the need to organise people, motorbikes or helicopters for mustering operations.The technology is designed to operate without farmers having to pilot the drones themselves.Rogers told Forbes Australia that the system responds to the movement of the herd and makes decisions in real time. He said, “Instead of piloting, the farmer simply sets the task and the system executes it, making decisions in real time based on how the herd moves, then reporting back everything it sees.”GrazeMate’s system is designed to collect information about farm conditions alongside moving livestock. The drones can report on available pasture, provide estimates of herd weight and assess critical infrastructure, including water troughs. This information is intended to help farmers understand the condition of their land and livestock while carrying out routine management tasks.Rogers said the technology enables farmers to gather information while the drones are mustering cattle. The company’s approach combines livestock movement with data collection, allowing farmers to assess the paddock and the herd as part of the same operation. The system is intended to reduce the need for farmers to manage separate processes for moving cattle and checking farm conditions.GrazeMate has secured commitments for a $1.2 million pre-seed funding round led by Y Combinator, with Australia’s NextGen Ventures and Antler also participating. The funding comes as the company prepares to expand beyond its existing operations in Queensland and New South Wales into California.GrazeMate had commitments to muster 1.7 million acres of land across Queensland and New South Wales. The company’s expansion into California marks its move into the United States market. The funding round supports the startup’s development as it seeks to bring its autonomous livestock-mustering technology to additional farming operations.Rogers formalised GrazeMate as a company in 2025 and moved from working as a farmer to leading the business as its chief executive. He is also a mechatronics engineering student at the University of Sydney. NextGen Ventures discovered Rogers through its network of campus investors in 2025 before participating in the funding round.NextGen Ventures partner Jerry X’Lingson told Forbes Australia that Rogers had taught himself to code in Chinese while working with alternative drones because he could not initially afford the highest-specification models he later went on to build with. X’Lingson also described Rogers’s earlier engineering and artificial intelligence projects, including building a robotic arm at the age of 14 and training an AI model to detect electronic waste.Rogers’s experience recovering from serious injuries also contributed to his decision to build the company. He suffered a spinal tumour and a broken back, underwent three spinal surgeries and later travelled to Nepal to climb in the Everest region. X’Lingson described the experience by saying, “At 16, [founder Sam Rogers] faced a life-threatening spinal injury. After three spinal surgeries, he climbed Everest. ”Rogers told Forbes Australia that observing how Sherpas moved yaks in the Himalayas influenced his thinking about livestock management. He recalled how the herders would climb a hill and ring a bell, allowing the sound to travel through the valley and signal the herd to move. He said, “We’ve been working on how to replicate that kind of natural signalling on a much larger scale ever since.”Rogers attributed GrazeMate’s development to improvements in drone battery life, advances in artificial intelligence and changes in regulations governing autonomous systems. He told Forbes Australia that defence investment had driven improvements in drone batteries over the previous decade, while advances in AI had made edge computing more powerful and affordable.He also identified regulatory changes as a factor in the development of autonomous drone operations. Rogers said these developments were occurring as ranchers faced labour shortages, rising costs and increasing demand. GrazeMate’s system is designed to apply autonomous technology to livestock management, combining drone-based mustering with the collection of information about herds, pasture and farm infrastructure.With its $1.2 million pre-seed funding round and expansion plans for California, GrazeMate is developing its autonomous cattle-mustering system beyond its initial operations in Queensland
Article Summary: A 19-year-old Australian farmer’s son has developed an autonomous drone system to move cattle. His startup, GrazeMate, has raised $1.2 million in pre-seed funding to support its expansion into California. Founded by Sam Rogers, the company uses drones that farmers can operate through a mobile app to guide herds between paddocks without manually piloting the aircraft.

Article Title: MrBeast invests $250,000 for 55% stake in AI-powered Ball 2 on Shark Tank
Article Text:
YouTuber MrBeast (Getty Images)

Shark Tank

MrBeast backs AI-powered Ball 2 with a $250,000 Shark Tank deal

Why MrBeast's Ball 2 investment faces questions over consumer demand

MrBeast has built a career on turning unusual ideas into viral sensations. Now, the YouTube star is betting that the same formula can sell an everyday object with an unexpected twist. During his debut on, Jimmy Donaldson backed Ball 2, an AI-powered toy that promises to make ordinary play more interactive. The $250,000 investment came despite doubts from other investors, who questioned whether technology alone could convince customers to choose this ball over countless cheaper alternatives. The deal puts MrBeast's marketing instincts to the test, with the product's future depending on whether its novelty can attract lasting demand.Entrepreneurs Andrew Brown and Kevin Langdon pitched Ball 2 as a new take on a familiar toy. Unlike a standard foam ball, their product contains sensors that track its movement when users roll, throw or bounce it. The data connects to a companion app, where artificial intelligence can help create games based on how people use the ball.The idea aims to turn simple physical activity into an interactive experience. Instead of relying on a fixed set of rules, players can use the app to introduce new challenges and change how they play.During a demonstration, MrBeast and fellow investor Lori Greiner competed to see who could shake the ball more. Donaldson won and appeared pleasantly surprised by the result.“It worked way better than I was expecting it to work,” said Donaldson after getting his shake on, “that was cool.”His enthusiasm stood out as several investors questioned the product's appeal. Kevin Langdon even acknowledged the challenge of selling something that looks like an ordinary ball on a shop shelf.“If you put this next to another ball on a shelf it’s a tough sell,” admits Langdon.MrBeast ultimately offered $250,000 for a 55% stake in the company. The cousins accepted, celebrating the deal with a shout of “beast ball!”The biggest challenge for Ball 2 may not be its technology. It is convincing families that they need it.Balls are familiar, affordable and easy to use. Adding sensors and AI may attract curious buyers, but parents will still want to know whether the extra features justify the price. The product must also offer enough variety to keep children interested after the initial excitement fades.Kevin O'Leary, known as Mr. Wonderful, remained unconvinced by the pitch. He warned that the product's success would depend on creating a viral moment. Greiner also questioned whether consumers would embrace the concept.That concern makes MrBeast's involvement especially important. His huge online audience and experience creating attention-grabbing videos could give Ball 2 the exposure it needs. A viral campaign could turn an unfamiliar toy into a popular gift, particularly among younger fans.However, attention does not always translate into repeat sales. The company must deliver an enjoyable experience, reliable performance and clear value for money. Online buzz can open the door, but customer satisfaction will determine whether the business lasts.Ball 2 now has a powerful backer, but its biggest test lies ahead. MrBeast has shown that he believes in the product's potential. Whether buyers share that confidence will decide if this unusual AI toy becomes a genuine hit or a short-lived internet sensation.
Article Summary: MrBeast backs Ball 2, an AI-powered toy that promises to make ordinary play more interactive. The $250,000 investment came despite doubts from other investors. The deal puts MrBeast's marketing instincts to the test, with the product's future depending on whether its novelty can attract lasting demand.

Article Title: In 2019, Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz paid $20.8 million for a glass-walled California cliff house that had originally been offered for $30 million; two years later, they revealed its transformation in
Article Text:
Engineering on the La Jolla cliffs

Curating an extensive art collection

A long-cherished dream realized

Living in a modern architectural icon

Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million (£16 million) in 2019. They paid nearly $10 million less than the original asking price before turning the oceanfront property into an art-filled family home. Known as the Razor House, the glass-and-concrete estate sits on a cliff in La Jolla, near San Diego, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. According to Architectural Digest, the 11,000-square-foot property was first listed for $30 million. The couple completed the purchase in late 2019. Two years later, the couple opened the doors of their cliffside home to show how they had turned the unusual building, which extends out over the landscape, into a peaceful retreat filled with art for themselves and their children.Designed by well-known architect Wallace E. Cunningham and completed in 2007, the Razor House takes its name from the sharp-edged coastal cliff where it stands. The building features sweeping curves, floor-to-ceiling glass walls and solid concrete beams that extend outward over the ocean.According to architectural records cited by Architectural Digest, building the home required major engineering work to secure its heavy concrete frame to the coastal bedrock.The house covers several levels linked by a glass elevator. Its design gives almost every room clear, uninterrupted views of the sea. The property has six bedrooms, a main living pavilion, an underground garage that can hold up to eight vehicles, a private cinema and a guest house. Outside, an infinity-edge swimming pool creates the impression that it drops straight into the ocean below.After Keys and Swizz Beatz, whose real name is Kasseem Dean, took ownership of the home, they worked with interior designer Kelly Behun to bring warmth and personal touches to its modern concrete spaces. The couple used the large walls and open gallery spaces to display important works from the Dean Collection. Their private art collection includes contemporary pieces by Black artists and creators from around the world. In a feature published by Architectural Digest in late 2021, Keys explained how the home's unusual shape and design influenced their choices of furniture and artwork. "When you choose a house like this, you have to respect its architecture," Keys told Architectural Digest during the home tour. "We wanted to make sure it felt like a home, not just a museum." The interiors now feature major works by Kehinde Wiley, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Gordon Parks and Nick Cave. The couple chose low-profile furniture covered in soft, textured materials such as velvet, wool and shearling. These pieces soften the exposed concrete surfaces without blocking the coastal views.Swizz Beatz revealed that he had used a picture of the Razor House as his phone's screensaver for eight years before buying it. He had admired Cunningham's architecture long before the property came up for sale. When the estate went into foreclosure and appeared on the market at a lower price in 2019, the couple moved quickly to buy it. "It's a place where you can sit and contemplate, write, and create," Swizz Beatz told Architectural Digest in the 2021 interview. He described the home as both a place for creative work and a comfortable family retreat. "It was meant to be our place of peace." The main living room, which the family calls the "Dreamland" room, features a custom piano. Keys regularly uses it to compose music while looking out over the Pacific coastline.Beyond serving as a private home, the Razor House has become a well-known part of popular culture. Its futuristic design and dramatic cliffside position have led many local residents and architecture fans to compare it to the fictional Malibu mansion of Marvel character Tony Stark. The estate also has large outdoor terraces, a rooftop entertainment deck with an outdoor kitchen and private paths leading towards the beach below. Custom lighting built into the concrete structure lights up the home after dark without creating glare on its floor-to-ceiling glass walls. Property records confirm that the $20.8 million sale ranks among the highest property sales ever recorded in La Jolla. The price reflects both the lasting value of Cunningham's architectural design and the continued appeal of coastal California real estate.
Article Summary: Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million in 2019. Known as the Razor House, the glass-and-concrete estate sits on a cliff in La Jolla, near San Diego, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The 11,000-square-foot property was first listed for $30 million.

Article Title: A Massachusetts couple cut trees from their own land to build barns for 20 rescued animals; horses saved from slaughter can live there without ever working again
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How a couple turned their Massachusetts property into a refuge for rescued animals

Rescued horses find lifelong sanctuary after facing the threat of slaughter

From abuse to safety, rescued horses begin new lives at the farm

Rescuing blind horses became a personal commitment

Rescued animals bring companionship and a sense of purpose to volunteers

Heidi’s work with deaf students continues alongside the farm

In Norton, Massachusetts, Heidi and Bobby Medas have turned their own property into Smokey Chestnut Farm, a nonprofit sanctuary where rescued horses and other animals can live without being expected to work or entertain people. Using timber cut from their land, Bobby built barns to house the farm’s 20 residents, including horses saved from kill pens and the threat of slaughter. As reported by CBS News, what began as Heidi’s commitment to horse rescue has grown into a community effort supported by more than 60 volunteers. As the farm approaches its 15th anniversary in 2027, its mission extends beyond animal welfare, offering people a place to connect and contribute.Heidi and Bobby established Smokey Chestnut Farm as a nonprofit, with Bobby putting his practical skills to work on the land. A retired employee of Norton’s highway department, he built the barns and other structures using timber cut from the property itself. The farm now houses 20 rescued animals, including horses, mules, alpacas and pigs.The couple, who have been married for 42 years, did not set out to become public figures in their community.Heidi had been drawn to horse rescue, and the work gradually became a shared commitment. More than 60 volunteers now help support the operation, alongside thousands of people who contribute to its efforts.The farm is generally visited by appointment or during fundraising events. Its public profile grew during the Covid-19 pandemic, when people looked for outdoor activities and places to spend time away from crowded indoor settings. The couple also began giving away compost produced at the property, bringing more people into contact with the work being done there.Smokey Chestnut Farm is approaching its 15th anniversary in 2027. For Bobby, the attention and support have meant adjusting to a role he might not once have chosen.Several of the farm’s horses were saved from kill pens, holding facilities where animals may be bought for onward transport to slaughterhouses, including those in Canada and Mexico. The costs of rescuing a horse extend beyond the purchase itself. Smokey Chestnut Farm must also cover transport and quarantine, with the final bill depending on the animal’s condition and the arrangements needed to bring it to safety.The scale of the wider problem is reflected in estimates from the US Department of Agriculture, which put the number of horses from the United States slaughtered each year at between 18,000 and 25,000. Horses continue to be consumed as meat in several parts of the world, although slaughter for human consumption is not carried out legally within the United States.At Smokey Chestnut Farm, the animals are not expected to work or provide entertainment. Most do not wear harnesses, and there is no requirement for them to be ridden or trained. The intention is to provide care for the remainder of their lives, regardless of whether they can be handled easily or have any practical use to people.Hope and Faith, two Chincoteague ponies, remain wary of human contact. Heidi has described them as having been wild when they arrived, and they still prefer to keep their distance from people. They share their space with Lucky, a retired show pony whose former owners continue to visit. The older animal appears to have become a steady presence for the two ponies.Bonnie and Clyde, a pair of mules, were rescued from a kill pen in Pennsylvania. Clyde had suffered abuse before reaching the farm and initially spent much of his time standing in a corner, trembling. According to Heidi, his behaviour has improved since then. The pair live alongside Lucas, a large horse that was removed from an animal abuse case.Other residents have been surrendered for different reasons. Whiskey, a thoroughbred, was given up after failing to make money for his owner. Zilla, a Standardbred, had pulled a racing cart and worked with Amish families before being placed at risk of slaughter. Heidi received a call about Zilla and arranged for his rescue.When Zilla first arrived, he was frightened of people. Five years later, he had become comfortable in his surroundings. Heidi has described the change as a gradual process in which he came to recognise that he was safe.Two of the horses at the farm, Grace and Dakota, are blind. Dakota’s rescue began after Heidi received a video from a stranger showing the horse in a kill pen in Texas. She initially did not want to watch it, but her concern for the animal eventually led her to act.Dakota’s case also became part of a wider effort to save Kelsey, another blind horse who has since died. Heidi was determined to secure help for both animals, despite the practical and financial demands involved. Their stories reflect the farm’s policy of accepting animals on the basis of their need for care rather than their ability to be trained, ridden or used for work.The couple cannot take in every horse that needs rescuing. Smokey Chestnut Farm is currently full, meaning new arrivals must be accommodated elsewhere if they are to be saved. Fundraising therefore remains important even when the farm itself has no available space.Heidi has worked to build relationships with other rescuers so that a horse can still be helped when there is no room in Norton. One of those partnerships is with Annie Crosby, an animal rescuer based in Rehoboth, Massachusetts. The two have now rescued six horses together.The sanctuary has also become an important place for people who spend time there. Crystal Medeiros, who volunteers at least four days a week, has found a particular connection with Zilla. Now retired, she has been able to pursue her longstanding wish to work with animals.Medeiros has spoken about the sense of peace she experiences at the farm and the relationships she has formed there. Caring for the animals gives her a routine built around practical tasks and attention to their needs. It also provides regular contact with people who share her interests.Annie Crosby, who also works as a therapist, has observed how time spent around horses can affect people. Her experience at the farm and through rescue work has shown her that the benefits are not confined to the animals themselves. The relationships formed around their care can matter to those involved, too.Animal welfare is not Heidi’s only long-standing commitment. For more than 30 years, she has worked as an interpreter for deaf students at Boston University, transcribing lecture notes in real time so that students can follow their classes.She has spoken about the demands faced by students with disabilities and her admiration for those who continue to pursue their education despite the obstacles they encounter. The work has given her another way to provide practical support to people who need it.Her involvement in education and animal rescue may appear to be separate responsibilities, but both depend on close attention to others and an understanding that people and animals can need different kinds of assistance. At the farm, that means allowing a frightened horse to settle at its own pace. In the classroom, it means helping students access information as a lesson unfolds.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.
